findings.title: Missing License File
findings.explanation: The repository does not contain a license file or licensing terms specifying how the extension may be used or distributed. Under the review policy, missing distribution permission is a blocking admission requirement.
findings.suggestion: Add a LICENSE file (e.g., MIT, Apache 2.0, or similar) to the repository to grant clear distribution and usage permissions.

items.title: No license file or license terms anywhere in the repository

findings.title: No license file or license terms anywhere in the repository
findings.evidence:
CurveMaker
==========

3D Slicer scripted module to generage a curve from a list of fiducials.
findings.explanation: The repository listing contains only CMakeLists.txt, CurveMaker.png, README.md, CurveMaker/CMakeLists.txt, CurveMaker/CurveMaker.py, the icon and the Testing CMakeLists files; a case-insensitive search for 'license|copyright|BSD|MIT|apache' over all text files returned no matches. Without any license or copyright grant, users and the extension index have no permission to redistribute the module, so the distribution-permission admission requirement is unmet.
findings.suggestion: Add a LICENSE file (any OSI-approved or otherwise permissive license is acceptable) and a short copyright/license statement in README.md and/or the header of CurveMaker.py.

==========

3D Slicer scripted module to generage a curve from a list of fiducials.

items.title: distanceToPoint() returns a scalar that the caller unpacks as a tuple

findings.title: distanceToPoint() returns a scalar that the caller unpacks as a tuple
findings.evidence:
if self.CurvePoly == None:
      return numpy.Inf
findings.explanation: updateTargetFiducialsTable() does '(err, evec) = self.logic.distanceToPoint(pos, extrapolate)' (line 613). Before any curve has been generated CurvePoly is None, so distanceToPoint returns a float and the unpacking raises TypeError, breaking the Distance table as soon as a target markups node is selected before pressing 'Generate Curve'.
findings.suggestion: Return a tuple such as (float('inf'), numpy.zeros(3)) in the early-return branch, or handle the None-curve case in the caller.

findings.title: distanceToPoint returns a scalar where callers expect a tuple, causing TypeError
findings.evidence:
if self.CurvePoly == None:
        return numpy.Inf
findings.explanation: When no curve has been generated, distanceToPoint returns numpy.Inf. updateTargetFiducialsTable unpacks the result into (err, evec), so it raises TypeError. This happens when the user selects a target fiducial list while the source curve is absent, for example after the Source selector is set to None. The GUI callback fails with an unhandled exception.
findings.suggestion: Return a tuple, for example `return (numpy.Inf, numpy.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]))`, and fix the caller's unpacking accordingly.

items.title: setup() assumes a 3D view exists and crashes in layouts without one

findings.title: setup() assumes a 3D view exists and crashes in layouts without one
findings.evidence:
layout = slicer.app.layoutManager()
    view = layout.threeDWidget(0).threeDView()
    renderer = layout.activeThreeDRenderer()
    self.scalarBarWidget.SetInteractor(renderer.GetRenderWindow().GetInteractor())
findings.explanation: When the module is opened while the current layout has no 3D view (for example 'Red slice only' or a custom slice-only layout), layoutManager.threeDWidget(0) returns None, so .threeDView() raises AttributeError during setup() and the module panel fails to build. The scalar bar is also bound to whichever 3D view happened to be first, and is never re-bound or detached.
findings.suggestion: Guard the 3D-view lookup (skip scalar-bar setup when no 3D view is available) and attach the scalar bar lazily when curvature display is enabled, or use the view's own renderer via a layout observer.

items.title: Division by zero for coincident control points in curvature and spline code

findings.title: Division by zero for coincident control points in curvature and spline code
findings.evidence:
for i in range(1,n-1):
        p = numpy.array(points.GetPoint(pts.GetId(i+1)))
        ds = numpy.linalg.norm(p-pp)
        T  = (p-pp) / ds
findings.explanation: computeCurvatures divides by ds, the distance between consecutive points, without checking for zero. Two identical adjacent fiducials give a NaN or ZeroDivisionError during curvature updates. This is an ordinary robustness bug.
findings.suggestion: Skip or merge duplicate points before computing tangents, and guard the division.

items.title: Icon file present but not installed through CMake resources

findings.title: Icon file present but not installed through CMake resources
findings.evidence:
set(MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES
  )
findings.explanation: CurveMaker/Resources/Icons/CurveMaker.png exists, but MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES is empty, so the icon is not installed with the module. The module's icon depends on the external URL in the root CMakeLists instead.
findings.suggestion: Add Resources/Icons/CurveMaker.png to RESOURCES, or delete the unused file.

items.title: Minimum curvature is always reported as 0 or below

findings.title: Minimum curvature is always reported as 0 or below
findings.explanation: minKappa is initialized to 0.0 and kappa is a norm, so it is never negative. Its update is therefore never triggered, so the 'Minimum' readout in the GUI always shows 0. The max branch is also an elif, so a value that lowers the minimum cannot also raise the maximum. Users relying on the min/max readouts get wrong values.
findings.suggestion: Initialize minKappa and maxKappa from the first kappa value (or to +/-inf), and use two independent `if` statements.

items.title: No documentation, tutorial, sample data or tests; overlaps MarkupsToModel

findings.title: No documentation, tutorial, sample data or tests; overlaps MarkupsToModel
findings.evidence:
CurveMaker
==========

3D Slicer scripted module to generage a curve from a list of fiducials.
findings.explanation: The only documentation is a two-line README (with a typo); there is no tutorial, no sample markups, no screenshots in the repository and no working test. The core function (fit a curve through markups and render it as a tube) is already provided by the MarkupsToModel extension, so users have no guidance on when to prefer this module.
findings.suggestion: Add a README with usage steps and a sample .mrk.json, and state the difference from MarkupsToModel.

items.title: No functional tests; test module commented out

findings.title: No functional tests; test module commented out
findings.evidence: #slicer_add_python_unittest(SCRIPT ${MODULE_NAME}ModuleTest.py)
findings.explanation: The only test wiring is a commented-out line in Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt, and the in-script unittest is not exercised by CMake. Regressions such as the distanceToPoint and curvature bugs above would not be caught by CI.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test that exercises the logic class (nodeToPoly, distanceToPoint, computeCurvatures) without the GUI, and register it with slicer_add_python_unittest.

items.title: Registered unittest does not exist in the module script

findings.title: Registered unittest does not exist in the module script
findings.evidence:
# Register the unittest subclass in the main script as a ctest.
  # Note that the test will also be available at runtime.
  slicer_add_python_unittest(SCRIPT ${MODULE_NAME}.py)
findings.explanation: CurveMaker.py imports unittest (line 2) but defines no unittest.TestCase subclass, and CurveMaker/Testing/Python/CMakeLists.txt has its test commented out. The generated ctest therefore has nothing to run and will fail or silently pass, so the extension has no automated coverage.
findings.suggestion: Add a CurveMakerTest(unittest.TestCase) class exercising nodeToPoly/calculateLineLength/distanceToPoint, or remove the registration.

items.title: Tag used before assignment in target-fiducials handler

findings.title: Tag used before assignment in target-fiducials handler
findings.evidence:
if self.targetFiducialsNode and self.tag:
        self.targetFiducialsNode.RemoveObserver(self.tag)
findings.explanation: onTargetFiducialsSelected reads self.tag, which is only assigned in setup when a target node is chosen. This works only because targetFiducialsNode is None initially. It is fragile: self.tag is never initialized in setup, so any change to that guard can raise AttributeError.
findings.suggestion: Initialize self.tag = None in setup() alongside targetFiducialsNode.

items.title: Unbound nnvec when two consecutive curve points coincide

findings.title: Unbound nnvec when two consecutive curve points coincide
findings.evidence:
norm = numpy.linalg.norm(nvec)
      if norm != 0:
        nnvec = nvec / norm

      # Calculate the distance between the point and the segment
      mag2 = 0.0

      op = npoint - p1
      aproj = numpy.inner(op, nnvec)
findings.explanation: If a segment has zero length (duplicate control points, or a spline that produces repeated samples), nnvec is never assigned and numpy.inner(op, nnvec) raises UnboundLocalError, aborting the distance table update. computeCurvatures() has the analogous division by ds without a zero check (lines 906-909).
findings.suggestion: Skip zero-length segments (continue) or initialise nnvec to a zero vector and guard the divisions.

items.title: cleanup() does nothing, leaving observers and the scalar bar attached

findings.title: cleanup() does nothing, leaving observers and the scalar bar attached
findings.evidence:
def cleanup(self):
    pass
findings.explanation: Observers are added to the source markups node, the destination model node and its display node (lines 407, 426, 429, 578) but never removed when the module widget is closed or the scene is closed. The observers keep references to the widget's Python methods, so later node modifications can call into a half-destroyed widget, and the vtkScalarBarWidget stays registered with the 3D view interactor.
findings.suggestion: Remove all observer tags and disable the scalar bar widget in cleanup(), and reset the stored node references.

findings.title: Observers are not removed on cleanup; stale state is kept on source deselection
findings.explanation: cleanup() is an empty pass, so PointModifiedEvent and ModifiedEvent observers registered on the Markups/Model nodes persist when the module is closed or reloaded. Separately, onSourceSelected does not reset tagSourceNode or self.logic.SourceNode when the selector is cleared, so a later callback can act on a removed node. This can cause duplicate or stale updates.
findings.suggestion: Implement cleanup() to call RemoveObserver for all stored tags, and reset the tags and node references when the selection is cleared.

findings.title: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.9) is rejected by CMake 4
findings.evidence: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 2.8.9)
findings.explanation: CMake 4.x removed compatibility with cmake_minimum_required values below 3.5 and errors out, so the extension cannot be configured on a modern build machine unless the Slicer superbuild injects CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM.
findings.suggestion: Raise the minimum to a version supported by current Slicer builds (e.g. 3.16 or higher).

findings.title: Pinned to branch 'master' and documentation is minimal
findings.evidence: set(EXTENSION_HOMEPAGE "https://www.slicer.org/slicerWiki/index.php/Documentation/Nightly/Extensions/CurveMaker")
findings.explanation: scm_revision is 'master', a moving branch, so the reviewed code can change without a catalog update. The README is three lines, with no usage instructions, sample data, or tutorial, and it points to an outdated wiki URL in CMakeLists.txt. This limits how well users can adopt the module.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to a tagged commit, and add usage documentation and a link to a working homepage.

items.title: numpy.Inf removed in NumPy 2 breaks distance computation

findings.title: numpy.Inf removed in NumPy 2 breaks distance computation
findings.evidence: minMag2 = numpy.Inf
findings.explanation: numpy.Inf was deprecated in NumPy 1.20 and removed in NumPy 2.0; on a Slicer build shipping NumPy 2 the Distance table raises AttributeError. The same alias is used at line 1035.
findings.suggestion: Use float('inf') or numpy.inf.

items.title: Legacy Slicer-4 idioms and unused imports

findings.title: Legacy Slicer-4 idioms and unused imports
findings.evidence:
import os
import unittest
from __main__ import vtk, qt, ctk, slicer
import math
import numpy
findings.explanation: os, math and unittest are unused; 'from __main__ import ...' is the pre-Slicer-5 pattern (slicer.util / slicer.qSlicerWidget imports are preferred), and self.tag is never initialised in setup() (line 43 is commented out) although onTargetFiducialsSelected reads it at line 572. None of this changes behavior today but makes the module fragile.
findings.suggestion: Drop unused imports, initialise self.tag = None in setup(), and modernise the imports.

findings.title: Legacy Slicer 4 APIs and unused imports
findings.evidence:
import os
import unittest
from __main__ import vtk, qt, ctk, slicer
findings.explanation: The module uses `from __main__ import vtk, qt, ctk, slicer` and the PythonQt-style connect() calls, along with unused imports os and unittest. Compatibility with the current Slicer release was not verified. These are non-blocking, but they should be modernized.
findings.suggestion: Verify the module loads and runs on the current Slicer release, then replace the __main__ imports with explicit imports.
